title: System discovery and relay bootstrap contract
description: Reconstructed PSTF feature for the shared discovery contract rooted at `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` and the browser relay bootstrap path that consumes it. The approved slice covers sidecar-first public relay discovery, service-pubkey and feature-gate advertisement, control-plane kind advertisement, cached Nostr discovery loading, EOSE-bounded read-model bootstrap, transition into live subscriptions, and the discovery inputs consumed by public browser flows, encrypted browser gating, and signer-first operator relay discovery.
dependencies: A reachable Bahia relay sidecar or equivalent advertised public browser relay set
`Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` served by `internal/adapters/nostr/projector.go`
A Bahia service pubkey when canonical Bahia-authored read models or encrypted transport are in use
Nostr client subscribe/query support with explicit EOSE handling
Transport-policy decisions recorded in PSTF backlog decisions for public versus encrypted relay separation

actors.name: browser_shared_state_bootstrap
actors.role: loads Nostr discovery once, resolves relay bootstrap inputs, queries canonical read models until EOSE, and keeps live subscriptions open

actors.name: bahia_service
actors.role: publishes discovery metadata, owns the canonical service pubkey, and authors canonical Bahia read-model and status/result events

actors.name: encrypted_browser_consumers
actors.role: use system discovery to decide whether encrypted request/result transport is available and which relay set is safe for sensitive traffic

actors.name: operator_cli
actors.role: falls back to `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` for relay discovery after explicit flags and environment variables

in_scope: `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` advertisement of sidecar-first public browser relay bootstrap fields (`nostr.browser_relays`, `nostr.sidecar_url`)
Advertisement of `nostr.service_pubkey` and `features.relay_read_models` required by shared browser read-model bootstrap
Advertisement of `nostr.browser_encrypted_request_relays` and `features.encrypted_nostr_requests` as discovery inputs for encrypted browser domains
Advertisement of `control_plane.version`, capabilities, request/status/result/read-model kind maps, correlation tags, and MCP async-correlation metadata
Shared browser Nostr discovery caching, concurrent-load dedupe, and force-reload behavior
Shared browser control-plane bootstrap behavior: fail closed unless relay-read-model capability is advertised, query until EOSE, then transition into live subscriptions
Canonical-author filtering for Bahia-owned read models and status/result activity once the service pubkey is known
Signer-first operator relay discovery fallback from `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` using `browser_relays` plus `sidecar_url`
out_of_scope: Public command publication semantics for specific service/deployment, adoption/runtime, Soul Factory, or LLM actions beyond their dependence on the discovery contract
Encrypted request/result payload semantics for notifications, orgs, payments, secrets, run logs, or other encrypted operations beyond discovery and relay separation
Legacy REST/SSE/JWT/browser-auth exchanges as normative product behavior
Direct `nostr.relays` discovery as an approved browser bootstrap contract when the sidecar is disabled
Release-specific transport governance beyond the discovery contract itself

summary: `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` returns a wrapped `data` payload containing registry, Nostr, control-plane, runtime, OCI, Blossom, and feature information.
When sidecar mode is enabled, the handler advertises `nostr.browser_relays` and `nostr.sidecar_url`; when sidecar mode is disabled, the handler currently exposes `nostr.relays` instead.
The handler derives `nostr.service_pubkey` and `nostr.service_npub` from the configured service private key when available.
`features.relay_read_models` is currently true only when the sidecar is enabled and Nostr publication is enabled.
`features.encrypted_nostr_requests` is currently true only when browser encrypted-request relay URLs, backend encrypted-request relay URLs, and a service private key are all configured.
`web/src/lib/stores/system.svelte.js` caches the first successful Nostr discovery load, deduplicates concurrent loads, and supports explicit force reload.

`web/src/lib/stores/controlplane.svelte.js` resolves browser relays from `browser_relays` plus `sidecar_url`, falls back to `nostr.relays` only if those are absent, requires `features.relay_read_models`, queries the relay until EOSE, applies replaceable latest-wins semantics, and then keeps a live subscription open.
The shared control-plane store rejects canonical Bahia read-model and status/result events when they are not authored by the advertised Bahia service pubkey.

The operator CLI resolves relays from `--relay`, then `BAHIA_NOSTR_RELAYS`, then `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` using `browser_relays` and `sidecar_url`; it does not use `nostr.relays` from system discovery.

questionable_or_legacy_behavior.behavior: The handler still exposes `nostr.relays` when the sidecar is disabled, and the browser helper can normalize that field if present.

summary: `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` is the authoritative discovery contract for relay-backed shared browser state and related consumer gating.
The approved bootstrap contract is sidecar-first: browser public relay discovery comes from `nostr.browser_relays` and `nostr.sidecar_url`, not from raw `nostr.relays` exposure.
The shared browser bootstrap path must fail closed unless `features.relay_read_models=true` and at least one browser relay URL is advertised.

The browser must load Nostr discovery once per bootstrap cycle, deduplicate concurrent loads, and avoid per-store refetching of the same discovery payload unless a force reload is explicitly requested.

After discovery, the browser must query canonical read models and recent activity/status through scoped relay filters, wait for EOSE to complete historical catch-up, and then remain subscribed for realtime updates.
Canonical Bahia read models and status/result activity must be filtered by the advertised Bahia service pubkey once that pubkey is known.

Sensitive encrypted browser flows must derive availability only from `nostr.browser_encrypted_request_relays`, `nostr.service_pubkey`, and `features.encrypted_nostr_requests`, while keeping those relay URLs separate from public browser relays.
`control_plane` kind advertisement is part of the intended discovery contract because browser public flows, encrypted browser flows, MCP async consumers, and LLM/operator consumers all depend on it.

approved_decisions.effect: Direct `nostr.relays` exposure when the sidecar is disabled is not part of the intended discovery behavior for this slice and should be fixed or removed rather than preserved.

preconditions: The browser or client can reach `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)`.
When public relay-backed shared state is intended, the deployment advertises sidecar-first browser relay URLs and `features.relay_read_models=true`.
When canonical Bahia read-model filtering is intended, the deployment has a service key so `nostr.service_pubkey` is advertised.
When encrypted browser transport is intended, both browser and backend encrypted-request relay sets are configured and a service key is present.
postconditions: A conforming browser bootstrap resolves its relay inputs and Bahia service pubkey from `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` without hidden per-feature discovery calls.
Historical shared state is loaded through relay queries bounded by EOSE before the client transitions into live subscriptions.
Public and encrypted relay sets remain distinct in the discovery contract.
Consumers that depend on control-plane kinds can subscribe using the advertised kind maps and correlation tags rather than out-of-band constants alone.

happy_paths.title: Shared browser bootstrap discovers sidecar-first relays and becomes live after EOSE
steps: Browser loads `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` and caches the result
Browser resolves relay URLs from `nostr.browser_relays` plus `nostr.sidecar_url` and reads `nostr.service_pubkey`
Browser connects to the advertised relay set, queries canonical read models plus recent activity until EOSE, applies latest-wins/tombstone behavior, and then opens live subscriptions

happy_paths.title: Encrypted browser domains use discovery only to gate encrypted transport
steps: Browser loads `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)`
Browser enables encrypted request/result flows only when those encrypted discovery inputs are coherently advertised and keeps them separate from public browser relay URLs

happy_paths.title: Operator CLI falls back to system discovery after explicit relay inputs
steps: Operator CLI checks `--relay` first and `BAHIA_NOSTR_RELAYS` second
If neither is present, CLI loads `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)`
CLI resolves relays from `browser_relays` plus `sidecar_url` and uses those for signer-first operator requests

failure_paths.title: Relay read models not advertised
failure_paths.behavior: If `features.relay_read_models` is false, the shared browser bootstrap fails locally instead of silently falling back to unsupported shared-state behavior

failure_paths.title: No browser relays advertised
failure_paths.behavior: If no browser relay URLs are advertised for the sidecar-first path, the shared browser bootstrap fails closed with a deterministic discovery error

failure_paths.title: No relay accepted connection during bootstrap
failure_paths.behavior: If the browser cannot connect to any advertised browser relay, bootstrap fails and shared state does not claim readiness

failure_paths.title: Encrypted transport incompletely configured
failure_paths.behavior: If only public browser relays are present, or browser/backend encrypted relay sets or the service key are incomplete, encrypted transport remains unavailable and must not be inferred from public discovery fields

edge_cases: Concurrent `loadSystemInfo()` calls must deduplicate to a single fetch.
Force reload must refresh cached Nostr discovery state rather than returning stale discovery metadata.
Canonical Bahia events from non-service authors must be ignored after the service pubkey is known.
Replaceable read models must obey latest-wins and tombstone semantics by `(kind, pubkey, d-tag)`.
System discovery must continue advertising removed legacy feature flags as explicit `false` values so old clients fail closed.
Kind advertisement for optional domains such as LLM must disappear when the corresponding feature is disabled.
non_functional_requirements: Bootstrap must remain event-driven: historical catch-up is bounded by EOSE and live subscriptions stay open afterward.
Public relay discovery and encrypted relay discovery must remain separate security boundaries.
System discovery must be cacheable and deterministic enough that multiple consumers can share one payload instead of independently probing transport state.
The discovery contract must be specific enough that downstream consumers do not need to guess control-plane kind ids or legacy-surface availability.

contradictions_and_gaps.note: `docs/api.md` omits `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` even though product docs, code, tests, and other PSTF slices treat it as a hard bootstrap contract.
The handler still exposes `nostr.relays` when sidecar mode is disabled, but the approved intended contract for this slice is sidecar-first and explicitly excludes that fallback.

Current selected tests prove local browser bootstrap behavior and local control-plane state handling, but the portfolio still lacks one multi-consumer contract test showing a single `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` payload satisfies public browser bootstrap, encrypted browser gating, and operator CLI discovery together.
